planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial to full shade; Bush Flax is frost-hardy once established, more cold-tolerant than many New Zealand natives.

directions: Plant in partial to full shade in humus-rich, consistently moist soil; Bush Flax is a clump-forming New Zealand forest-floor native reaching 4-5 feet, with silvery-backed arching leaves, fragrant yellow-green flowers, and orange berries. It is frost-hardy once established, making it more cold-tolerant than many other New Zealand natives, and suits a shaded woodland garden where its architectural strap-leaf form contrasts well with broader-leaved shade perennials.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Shore Astelia tolerates coastal wind and moderate frost once established.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained soil; Shore Astelia forms dense, silver-grey strap-leaf clumps to about 4 feet tall and wide, a coastal New Zealand species that is wind-tolerant and moderately frost-hardy. It colors up most vividly silver with more sun exposure than its shadier relative Astelia fragrans, making it a good choice for a sunnier spot in a New Zealand-themed garden where strong foliage texture is wanted.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into humus-rich, moist soil in full to partial shade, protected from direct sun and wind; Perching Lily is the most shade-demanding of the Astelia species offered here.

directions: Plant in full to partial shade, protected from direct sun and wind, in humus-rich, moist soil; Perching Lily is an epiphytic or terrestrial New Zealand forest native reaching 2-3 feet, with narrow, silvery-backed leaves up to several feet long and flowers that age to red or pink. It is the most shade-demanding of the New Zealand Astelia species, needing genuine forest-floor or understory conditions to thrive, and is generally sourced through specialty New Zealand native-plant nurseries rather than general retail.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Lemonwood is the straight species, distinct from the already-grown variegated cultivar.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade in well-drained soil; Tarata is a fast-growing New Zealand native tree reaching 8-12 meters in the wild (smaller in cultivation), with glossy, lemon-scented foliage and small yellow flowers in spring. It tolerates part shade, though foliage density is best in full sun, making it a versatile screening or specimen tree for a mild-winter garden. This straight species is distinct from the already-grown variegated 'Variegatum' cultivar.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Ralph's Karo is drought-, wind-, and frost-tolerant once established, widely used for hedging in New Zealand.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained soil; Ralph's Karo is an evergreen New Zealand shrub to small tree reaching 4-6 meters, with silvery-toned leathery leaves and dark-red spring and summer flowers. It is widely planted in New Zealand for hedging and screening, tolerating drought, wind, and frost well once established, though it becomes more open and spindly when grown in deeper shade compared to full sun.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Taupata is the straight species, distinct from the already-grown patented 'Tequila Sunrise' cultivar.

directions: Plant in full sun to full shade in well-drained soil; Taupata is a ubiquitous New Zealand coastal native with glossy, rounded leaves, growing from a dense shrub in open exposure to a small tree in sheltered sites, reaching 8 feet to 25 feet depending on conditions. It is genuinely shade-tolerant across its full light range, salt- and wind-tolerant, and frost-hardy once mature, making it a versatile hedging or screening plant for coastal or Mediterranean-climate gardens. This straight species is distinct from the already-grown patented golden-variegated 'Tequila Sunrise' cultivar.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Five Finger performs best under a shaded canopy despite tolerating sun and wind.

directions: Plant under a shaded canopy or in full sun in well-drained soil; Five Finger is one of the most commonly grown New Zealand native garden and houseplant trees, fast-growing to 13-20 feet, with glossy, palmate leaves divided into five finger-like leaflets. It performs best under shade though it tolerates sun and wind reasonably well, and shows moderate frost tolerance once established. Its striking foliage shape makes it a popular architectural accent in both shaded garden beds and large containers.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into cool, moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Orihou can become leggy in very deep shade, so bright shade is ideal.

directions: Plant in partial to full shade in cool, moist, well-drained soil; Orihou is a New Zealand shrub to small tree reaching 6-12 feet, with leathery, glossy leaflets held in hand-like clusters, cream flowers, and dark purple berries. It prefers cool, sheltered, shaded sites typical of mountain forest understory, though it can become leggy in very deep shade, so bright dappled light is ideal. It is sold by native specialty nurseries for forest-garden underplanting projects.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a sturdy support in full sun to part shade; Akatea needs a sheltered, frost-free site to establish well.

directions: Plant against a sturdy support in a sheltered, frost-free site in full sun to part shade; Akatea is a vigorous New Zealand native climbing vine, reaching 20-33 feet given support, with glossy foliage and masses of white, star-shaped summer flowers that are popular with native bees. It tolerates part shade and, once established, moderate frost and drought, distinct from the already-grown pohutukawa (Metrosideros excelsa), which is a tree rather than a climbing vine.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Supplejack is a tough forest understory climber, sourced through native specialty or restoration nurseries.

directions: Plant in partial to full shade in moist, well-drained soil; Supplejack is a tough evergreen forest vine endemic to New Zealand's North and South Islands as well as Stewart and the Chatham Islands, growing up to 60 feet in the wild with rapid summer growth and red berries present year-round that are valued by native birds. It is a classic shade/understory climber of New Zealand forests, well suited to a shaded woodland garden wanting an authentic native climbing component. It is generally sourced through native specialty or restoration nurseries rather than general retail.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into free-draining soil in full sun; Native Broom is a true sun-loving species, not a shade plant despite otherwise accompanying New Zealand shade natives in this batch.

directions: Plant in full sun in free-draining soil; Native Broom is an evergreen New Zealand shrub with flattened, leafless, photosynthetic stems (cladodes) rather than true leaves, bearing masses of small purple-mauve flowers from spring through summer. It tolerates drought, wind, and coastal exposure well, and some partial shade, but genuinely prefers full sun rather than functioning as a shade plant. Its unusual leafless, jointed stem structure makes it a conversation-piece addition to a xeriscape or New Zealand-themed sunny border.
